w: Swamishri was recuperating from his illness. He was advised to take maximum rest, yet he spent time reading and answering letters from devotees. Sometimes, a conversation would follow and Swamishri would talk on the subject.

Someone praised the patient nature of a sadhu who looks after the administration of a mandir. Swamishri added,"One who administrates has to be calm and very patient. He also has to be tolerant and friendly with everyone. Even when meeting or talking to someone, he has to be polite and proper."
From 10.00am to 12.30pm and also in the evening, Swamishri was engaged in an emergency meeting with senior sadhus to further the BAPS earthquake relief activities.
Today's national paper, 'The Sydney Morning Herald', carried a story of the murti pratishtha ceremony: 'Divine visitors bears blessings for the gods of Rosehill.'

"In his 81st year, he seems an improbable empire-builder. But millions of devotees, more than 8,000 branch offices and 680 sadhu disciples can't all be wrong… And yesterday, His Divine Holiness, who holds the world record for the most temples consecrated clocked up his 411th, bestowing his blessings on the newly installed marble gods at the Rosehill temple."
At 4.55 p.m., the Vedic rituals of Vastu yagna was held for the Mandir Prasad Pravesh (entry into the mandir).
After the Vastu rituals, Swamishri declared open the Swaminarayan Primary School at Abu for boys from Kindergarten to Grade 5.
In the evening assembly Swamishri honored Pujya Mahant Swami and sadhus who had returned after a Satsang tour abroad. (For details see News report)

Harshadbhai Rana, a devotee from Nairobi, was highly impressed with the construction work of Akshardham. He expressed his admiration to Swamishri, " Bapa! I saw the ongoing construction of the Akshardham complex. You have performed a miracle and used your divine power."
Swamishri replied, " It is due to the power of Shriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj and the efforts of sadhus and devotees. Is it possible to do it single-handedly!"
"But things are getting done due to your inspiration," Harshadbhai added.

"The inspiration comes from up there that the mandir should be done here." Swamishri performed the exact action in the poster of Yogiji Maharaj pointing to the land on the banks of the Yamuna. "It is he who is inspiring that the mandir be made here (same action again). He had written again and again that the mandir be made here (repetition of action)."

Swamishri repeated the same action three times and emphasized that the work was being done through the divine wish and inspiration of Guru Yogiji Maharaj. The sadhus and devotees were impresed by Swamishri's total devotion to Yogiji Maharaj.

To please Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Guru Pramukh Swami Maharaj children, youths and senior devotees perform austerities, pilgrimages or other devotional means. The spiritual endeavors performed by the devotees during Swamishri's visit to the local centers are congratulatory and worthy of recognition. It also reflects Swamishri's divinity for inspiring such spiritual efforts in children, teenagers and devotees.
6 Feb 2003, New Delhi
16 BAPS youths motorcycled 4,644 km in 17 days from Chansad to Delhi.

ph: Swamishri ritually inaugurates the Swaminarayan Vidyapith Primary School that will officially begin this year at the BAPS Chhatralay in Abu
Shri Chandrakantbhai Trivedi is seen bowing and listening to Swamishri's blessings.

w: At 10.30 a.m., Swamishri traveled to the ‘Shri Bavis Gam Patidar Kelavani Mandal Boys Hostel’ on the Vidyanagar-Karamsad Road. After the pujan rituals Swamishri inaugurated the hostel and blessed the inaugural assembly.
During a meeting, a devotee showed his spectacles and said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "Bapa! I wonder if the number has changed? But I see faults in others!"
"If instead you put on the spectacles of God's glory, you will not see anyone's faults at all." In a few words, Swamishri spoke wonderfully about changing one's outlook.

During dinner, young volunteers were presenting various experiences before Pramukh Swami Maharaj. The youths also spoke of being insulted here and there during the Uttarayan zoli festival (collecting alms for the mandir). Pleased to learn that they had tolerated it, Swamishri said, "This too is a kind of training. You did well to come back without answering them. It was very good that you calmly bowed to them. Yogi Bapa and everyone have had such experiences. Our feeling is: 'Blessings to the one who gives, and good wishes to the one who does not.'"

After his morning walk, Pramukh Swami Maharaj sat on his bed to go to rest. Before lying down, Swamishri said, "Where is that young man?" Everyone began to think. Each person suggested a name in his own way. When Dilip's name came up, Swamishri said, "Yes, him." In this way Swamishri remembered him of his own accord and also praised his virtues. Swamishri said, "He has been here ever since Akshardham was built. He has great faith."

The next day, during the meetings, Dilip, whom Swamishri had remembered, also came. As soon as he saw him, Swamishri said lovingly, "You have come. I thought that since I did not see you, perhaps you had gone away. But he has faith. He has been here ever since (Akshardham) was built."
Dilip said, "And I want to finish my life right here."
Hearing this, Swamishri was pleased. (Dilip has served the Sanstha as an engineer for years.)

Today, in the "Balpravrutti Divya Sannidhi Parva", the programme "Iti Vachanamrutam" began. Sitting in front of Mahant Swami Maharaj's seat, a volunteer took the Vachanamrut in his hands and began to read: "Swaminarayan Hare... Vachanamrut Sarangpur 19, on fortune awakening."

The special feature of this programme was that this Vachanamrut was being newly added to the Sarangpur section. And as if this Vachanamrut was being created right then, the programmes were being presented according to the words in it.
As part of this programme, there was a question and answer session with Swamishri.
The first question was asked of Swamishri: "If our family members get in the way of our children's activities, what should we do?"
"Renounce them..." Hearing this unexpected, humorous answer, everyone burst out laughing.

Just then volunteers from Surat placed thals (plates) of various delicacies before Swamishri and began to perform arti. Swamishri at once pointed to Akshar Purushottam Maharaj and the guru parampara seated above.
Just then another question was asked: "Swami! What do we lose by not doing arti?"

Swamishri said, "Yogibapa used to say, 'At the time of arti, thal and chesta, Shriji Maharaj himself comes in person,' and if we are absent at that time, we miss the darshan of Shriji Maharaj. Even if we are present only physically, that is, even if we are not present in mind, still to obey what Shriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj have commanded is a great thing. So to gain that benefit, we must be present."

Just then youths entered doing dandvat (prostrations). They asked, "We feel bored of doing dandvat, we get tired, our faith does not last, yet you do so many dandvats even at this age. With what thought do you do them?"
"Glory!" Swamishri answered the big question in a single word. Short and sweet.
Just then devotees came doing a 'gabad yatra' (a rolling pilgrimage) and asked, "If we do spiritual practices such as a gabad yatra, do we get its fruit or not?"

Swamishri gave a beautiful answer: "If we do the practices of arti, thal, chesta and so on, as Shriji Maharaj has commanded us, then we get the fruit. Other rolling pilgrimages will just make us roll over, and we will not get the fruit."
The next question was asked of Swamishri: "You are Brahman. So how does the world appear to you?"
Swamishri said, "It appears divine."
In the next question it was asked, "The scriptures contain a great deal of knowledge, and we are from the villages, so how can we gain that knowledge?"

Giving a wonderful answer, Swamishri said, "There must be firm conviction in God. There should be no hollowness in it. All the scriptures are contained in that. Gunatitanand Swami too has said in his talks, 'One who has attained conviction has completed all spiritual practices, and nothing
remains to be done.' So we should make our conviction firm."
To clarify this, the next question was asked: "Only if our natures are removed will we see Shriji Maharaj in you?"
"Yes," Swamishri answered.
Then a question was asked: "If we have your darshan at the time of death, should we understand that Shriji Maharaj has come to take us?"

Swamishri confirmed this, but at the same time clarified further, saying, "He gives birth only where the Satpurush is." Even if we are not purified in this birth, he will give us the next birth in the company of the Satpurush, purify us and take us to Akshardham.

The next question asked: "Shriji Maharaj has said that the five entities are eternal. Among these five, you are Aksharbrahma and we are jivas (souls). Both are eternal. So did you meet us before this?"

Swamishri said, "This is the very first time that Shriji Maharaj and Swami have been met. Countless ages have passed. So now get to it. Do not waste even a second. Keep your eyes on Shriji Maharaj, Gunatitanand Swami and the Satpurush. Become absorbed in them."

A discussion arose about the four forms of Akshardham. One volunteer asked, "Which is the fourth? Because three we know. One is in Gandhinagar, the second in Delhi, the third is being built in America. So which is the fourth?"

The volunteer opposite explained, "This is not about the four forms of Akshardham, but the four forms of Akshar." Saying this, he explained, "One is as Chidakash, the second as Akshardham, which holds countless millions of muktas, and the third as the servant of Maharaj in Akshardham." Then Swamishri was asked, "Swami! Which is the fourth form?"
Smiling, Swamishri said, "You answer it yourself."
The volunteer said, "You! Isn't that right, Swami?"
With a smiling face Swamishri said, "Shriji Maharaj, Gunatitanand Swami and the Satpurush, it is a straight line understanding."

After that, using a balloon filled with air, a question was asked of Swamishri: "Just as a balloon stays firm when it is filled with air and goes limp when the air comes out, so when we listen to discourses at a shibir (camp) and when we have your company, everything stays fine, but afterwards it all goes flat. So please show us the way for our spiritual joy to remain unbroken till the end of the body."

Consoling them, Swamishri said, "It will remain. You do a lot of seva, devotion and so on, but this is not one day's work. Yogibapa used to say, 'Only after keeping satsang for a long time are doubts destroyed.' But everything will happen. If even a ghost does not let go, then Shriji Maharaj says, 'We want to make everyone brahmarup,' so how will he let go?"
One volunteer asked, "Will I have to take another birth?"
Swamishri said with spiritual joy, "This is the last birth."
Swamishri was asked, "Everyone's last birth?"
Swamishri said, "We are to have the company of the Satpurush birth after birth. So wherever we go, it is Akshardham. And we are already in that Akshardham."
Who but Aksharbrahma in person can give such a guarantee?!
The series of questions continued. Swamishri was asked, "What understanding should we keep so that problems of family and so on do not arise at all?"

Swamishri said, "Sankhya (understanding the perishable nature of the world). Because without sankhya, satsang is only half. We are attached to God because we have love; but if we cultivate sankhya, it becomes firm."
The volunteer spoke the final words: "Iti Vachanamrutam. Thus ends Sarangpur 19."
